title: In two CMIP6 models, standard CFC-12 transit-time ages on sigma0 26.5 rose about 5 yr more than true ideal age in 1994-2013; tracer-based ventilation shares of North Pacific AOU gains are unreliable
abstract: Question: campaign studies used CFC-12 and SF6 transit-time-distribution (TTD) ages on GLODAP lines to conclude that older water (less ventilation) explains most AOU gains on sigma0 26.5 near BATS and CalCOFI. Do these tracer ages give correct age changes? Approach: perfect-model test. We streamed CMIP6 CanESM5 (4 historical members, ssp245 to 2025, pre-industrial control) and MRI-ESM2-0 (1 member) from the Pangeo mirror, interpolated July fields to sigma0 26.5 and 26.7, and calculated CFC-12 and SF6 TTD ages with the observational method (inverse Gaussian, width/mean 1, 100 % saturation). We compared them with the model ideal age, which is the true mean age. We added an idealized steady-circulation test and applied the same code to GLODAPv2.2023 boxes. Results: for 1994-2013, cells with ideal age below 100 yr at 15-50 N had median CFC-12 age changes of +7.4 yr (CanESM5; true +2.7) and +7.1 yr (MRI-ESM2-0; true +1.5). In fixed cells the error drifted by +0.2 to +2.6 yr (North Atlantic water 5-15 yr old) and +6.9 to +18.1 yr (North Pacific water 15-40 yr old); SF6 drifted less (+0.7 to +6.7 yr in CanESM5). With true age, ventilation explained 0.67-1.60 of the model AOU change; with CFC-12 ages the ventilation part was 1.3-4.5 times too large (1.1-3.2 on 26.7). Sign agreement of AOU and age changes was 61 % even without forcing. In the idealized test, with no age change, a TTD width of 1.5-2 times the mean gave false increases of +2.5 to +8.3 yr, a constant 90 % saturation +3.8 to +9.0 yr and 30 % tracer-free water +13 to +22 yr. Observed North Pacific and CalCOFI age increases (+2.5 to +8.9 yr per decade) are of this size, but the fall-rise-fall of age near Bermuda (+3.7, -4.4, +5.9 yr) cannot come from a slow method error. CanESM5 reproduced the BATS loss (-3.0 to -11.1 vs -10.8 umol/kg, with ideal-age increases) but no model run had the CalCOFI decline or 2007-2025 step. Limitations: two models with unrealistic 26.5 water masses (CanESM5 too old, MRI-ESM2-0 too young), one MRI member without SF6 or scenario run, July fields, 18-27 extracted years per run, and a possible forcing-history mismatch. CMIP6 output is CC BY-SA 4.0, so model-derived tables and figures are regenerated by the code and not bundled.

citations.reason: Tests the tracer-age attribution of AOU gains with a perfect-model test; North Pacific age increases are within method-error size, Bermuda sign alternation is robust.
Ventilation fractions from CFC-12 ages can be too high by 1.1-4.5 times in models.
Agrees that saturation and TTD-shape errors make false CFC-12 age changes; quantifies them against true model age.
